TITLE — typeset this exact headline, large, high-contrast, in the vertical middle 60% of the frame. No other words, no byline, no watermark, no logo:
Make tmux survive a reboot, not just a disconnect

SUBJECT
tmux-resurrect and tmux-continuum bring your windows, panes, and working directories back after a reboot — but not the running processes. The honest setup.

NOTES
The survival subset sells one feature hard: a tmux session outlives the terminal. Lose the wifi, close the lid, reboot your router — and you're back. It sells that feature because it's true, right up to the word reboot . Reboot the machine tmux is running on — a kernel update, a crash, a you ran in the wrong window — and the tmux server dies with everything else. The session lives in that server's memory. No memory, no session. after a restart tells you the bad news flatly: That's the gap. tmux

ART DIRECTION

Draw the concrete apparatus this article is about — not a generic circuit board, robot, brain, or rocket. No faces. No UI chrome. No stock-tech collage. The still frame must read at 300px.
